rationale: Lens: scope, split and count honesty, round 4 at a593792a, re-read from disk (spec.md is the only file changed; the three ADR files are unchanged since 4c46cf64). My one round-3 ask (state and pin the plan-form follow-up case) is ADDRESSED by Ruling 2 with a stronger outcome than I proposed: the `<E>.7` follow-up is an informational N4 near-miss rather than a member, pinned by AC-1 row O, AC-2's 'no bd update recovery' leg, AC-4 (v), and the reworded OQ-7. The regression check of `git diff 4c46cf64 a593792a` in this lens is clean: the '129b' → 'follow-on spec (next free plain number)' rename changes no deliverable boundary (still five items; 129 still R1–R6 at 7–10 beads plus two documents; 130 still S0 + #233 + the rest of #251), and its justification is real — Background K's mechanism is exactly what `internal/approve/spec.go` `parseSpecID` (strconv.Atoi on the pre-hyphen text) and `FindEpicForBeadWithCache`'s `Sscanf("%d")` fallback do, and `bd show mindspec-wtjr` exists in the live database with that description (it is not in the tracked JSONL, which the consolidation says honestly). The #239 restatement is the one genuine narrowing this round, and it is stated, not slipped: Goal (d), Provenance, R4.2, AC-11 (i) and the Validation Proofs all say 'loud, named, recoverable by one audited command, not an automatic pass', the automatic-pass legs are removed rather than left as dead ACs, and the issue's own second ask ('the message should say so … the current wording asserts the merge does not exist') is met exactly. Two small honesty gaps remain, neither of which changes scope: the reattest-audited read-back does not say whether the Spec-125 revert/net-effect test still runs at read time on a fallback candidate (reattest runs it once, at reattest time), and R4.1's 'not a plan bead' vocabulary no longer matches R1.1's three-part definition. APPROVE with those two asks.
concrete_changes_required: State whether the reattest-audited read-back on a fallback candidate re-runs the R5(d) net-effect/revert test at the CURRENT tip. R4.2 says reattest 'runs every Spec-125 check' at acceptance time, but the two read-back conditions (binding names that merge SHA and second parent; binding carries a reattest audit whose scanned branch is this spec branch) say nothing about a later revert, and the round-3 'Unchanged machinery' bullet that carried the revert test was dropped. If the test runs, say so and add an AC-11 leg (accept via reattest, then revert the landing → MF-3 FAILS with the reverted sentence); if it does not, state that residual beside the forge residual.

Align R4.1 with R1.1's vocabulary: R4.1 (i) is `bead.PlanBeadIndex(E, D)` (plan-FORM only, deliberately wider than R1.1's plan-form + lineage + mapping), yet its hint sentence reads 'is linked to spec <S> by <disjunct> but is not a plan bead'. Say 'plan-form' where that is what is tested, and extend the override hint to a closed plan-form dependency that plan.md does not map (an N4 follow-up worked outside `mindspec next`), since that is now the most likely dependency to fail the landed-merge test for a benign reason.

findings.title: Round-3 ask status
findings.detail: F1r3.1 (plan-form follow-up under E is a member MF-1 always refuses; state and pin it; reword OQ-7) — ADDRESSED via Ruling 2, with a different and stronger outcome than I proposed: R1.1 now requires (c) N mapped by plan.md (MF-1's own `extractBeadSectionRaw`/`ParsePlanFrontmatter` mapping, read once per scoped call), so the `bd create --parent E` follow-up is not a member at all; it is the new informational class N4 ('a follow-up child of epic <E> that plan.md does not map (no Bead <N>); readiness would fail MF-1, so mindspec next does not select it'), never default-picked, with no claimable recovery, and an N4 positional goes to `GateReadiness` for MF-1's refusal with the scoped override as the deliberate route. Pinned by AC-1 row O (`<E>.7`, bug, parent E, unmapped → informational, 'never selected'), AC-2's O leg (no `bd update --parent` line offered), AC-4 (v) (an N4 follow-up present, exit 0, still named), and OQ-7 now says 'Such beads are by design never selectable, so failing on them would make every scoped next fail for as long as one follow-up stays open' — the sentence I asked to be corrected. R1.1 also cites two real examples in this repository (`mindspec-cter.8`, `mindspec-jfgj.4`, both bugs outside their plans). The rejected alternative (keep unmapped children as members, default-pick lifecycle first) is recorded with its reason. Net: 1 ADDRESSED, 0 PARTIAL, 0 MISSED; 2 NEW_ISSUE below, both minor.

findings.title: Regression check 4c46cf64..a593792a in this lens — clean; the #239 narrowing is stated, not slipped
findings.detail: Boundary and count: '129b' becomes 'the follow-on spec (next free plain number)' everywhere (Provenance, relief valve, Out of Scope, Non-Goals, OQ-1, grill); the five follow-on deliverables, 129's R1–R6 at 7–10 beads plus R7 and the ADR-0041 amendment, and 130's S0 + #233 + rest-of-#251 are unchanged. Background K's justification holds against the tree: `internal/approve/spec.go` `parseSpecID` does `strconv.Atoi(specID[:dashIdx])`, so `129b-…` yields spec_num 0, and `FindEpicForBeadWithCache` requires `num > 0` on the parent-epic path and then `Sscanf("%d")` on the title resolves 129 — a lettered successor's beads would resolve to THIS spec. `bd show mindspec-wtjr` exists (P2 bug, open, 2026-10-18) with that mechanism; the consolidation says plainly it is not yet in the tracked JSONL. #239: this round removes the automatic PASS on the fallback path after three rounds each produced a new false PASS (panel-only; stale-tip reset / forged sibling binding; empty-anchor revert mask). Every claim surface agrees — Goal (d) 'found and NAMED, and MF-3 fails loudly with the one audited command', Provenance 'fixed as loud, named, and recoverable by one audited mindspec reattest, not as an automatic pass', R4.2 'the automatic paths never accept a fallback candidate', AC-11 (i) 'recoverable, not auto-passed', and the Validation Proof runs ready-check → reattest → ready-check. #239's own text asked for either an ancestry-based pass OR a message that says what is true and does not send the operator to re-merge existing work; the second is met exactly and the first is deliberately refused with the evidence. No issue from the inherited cluster is dropped or re-homed silently this round. The R6.5 `ms-bead-impl` line is now correctly declared a staged rule under Decision 5's transition (target `next-action`, spec 133; date assigned when the rule table lands), which closes the last gap between the spec and the ADR it ships.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE — the audited read-back is silent on revert-awareness after acceptance
findings.detail: R4.2: 'An off-first-parent candidate is identified on later automatic reads iff two things hold: the bead's landed binding names exactly that merge SHA and second parent; the binding carries a reattest audit record whose scanned branch is this spec branch.' Nothing says the R5(d) net-effect/revert test (`landedContentSubsumedFn`/`landedRevertShapeFn` in internal/lifecycle/landed.go) runs on that read. On the primary path a binding-confirmed candidate still goes through it; the round-3 R4.2 bullet 'Same-second-parent grouping, the corroboration legs and the oldest-anchored revert/reapply test run unchanged' was replaced this round by 'Doc contracts' only. If the read-back skips the test, a landing that is accepted by reattest and later cleanly reverted PASSES MF-3 forever, which is the misattestation class Spec 125 R3 exists to refuse. This is a one-sentence statement either way plus one AC-11 leg; it is also the strongest answer to the round-4 forge question, because a forged audit on a real reachable merge still has to survive the content test at the tip. On the forge itself: `mindspec_landed_reattest_*` keys (reattest.go) and the binding are agent-writable bd metadata, so a forger with a real reachable `Merge bead/X` can convert 'FAIL → run reattest' into PASS and skip reattest's refusals (i) exactly-one-candidate and (ii) no-unreached-review; the spec states this residual and places it in the ADR-0037 §8 class, which is honest. The plan could cheaply narrow it by re-checking (i) at read time (the finder already enumerates candidates; require the audited merge to be the ONLY admitted candidate), which is deterministic and cannot deadlock; re-checking (ii) at read time can, so I do not ask for it.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE — R4.1's 'plan bead' no longer means what R1.1 means
findings.detail: R1.1 now defines a plan bead as plan-form ID + lineage E + plan.md mapping. R4.1 (i) tests only `bead.PlanBeadIndex(E, D)` (plan-form), deliberately wider for the fail-closed direction, which is right. But its hint sentence 'A metadata-only or non-plan member held to the test and failing it adds `<D> is linked to spec <S> by <disjunct> but is not a plan bead; if its work never landed as bead/<D>, override deliberately`' uses R1.1's term for R4.1's weaker test, and it does not fire for the dependency most likely to fail benignly under the new design: a closed, unmapped plan-form follow-up (N4) that was worked outside `mindspec next` and never merged under a `bead/<D>` subject. Say 'plan-form' where that is the test and extend the hint to the unmapped plan-form case.

findings.title: N4 and MF-1-mapped membership attacked — holds
findings.detail: (1) Selection and MF-1 read the same plan.md through the same mapping functions, so a member cannot fail MF-1 on mapping by construction, and an unmapped bead cannot be selected; the member set now equals 'beads GateReadiness can pass on MF-1 and lineage' as OQ-9 claims. (2) The parent-E shortcut is gone, so a parent-E row with a conflicting epic dependency that `FindEpicForBeadWithCache` returns first is N2c, not selected-then-refused; AC-1 row X pins it. (3) N2b's `bd update --parent E` recovery is safe for the reason given: in `FindEpicForBeadWithCache` the dependency loop runs before the title fallback, so adding the epic edge overrides a wrong `[NNN]` tag for readiness and complete too. (4) An all-N4 ready set with every lifecycle child closed exits 0 with 'impl approve' — consistent with spec 095's rule that non-lifecycle follow-ups never strand a spec short of review. (5) Cost: one `bd show` per plan-form row (the epic list cached) plus one plan.md read; a lineage read error or unreadable plan.md refuses the whole command rather than dropping rows. (6) The title fallback's degeneracies (duplicate spec_num → newest epic wins) still only produce a false blocking near-miss, never a false member, and Background K now records that nondeterminism with mindspec-wtjr.
